correctness.rationale: After ordering p,q (reversal only negates the commutator), tensoring with the rank-one constants projection on g coordinates gives the gcd reduction. For coprime m<n both projections are identical from cell to cell of length mn. On the n-block range in a cell, the squared defect from E_m is a sum over the distinct m-blocks straddling the boundaries jn. In each such block the two values have multiplicities r_j and m−r_j and are scaled by 1/√n, giving L/n exactly. The path has kernel the constants and simple eigenvalues by the first-row tridiagonal recurrence; independently, the weights are at most m/4 and the sum of squared nearest-neighbor differences is at most 4‖u‖², so μ_max≤m<n. For t=1−μ/n in (0,1), a unit range vector v of the compressed projection and (E_m v−tv)/√(t(1−t)) give one two-dimensional block, whose commutator eigenvalues are ±i√(t(1−t)). The other directions commute and constants ensure zero occurs. Repetition gives infinite multiplicities and essential norm equal to the finite-block norm. For n≡±1, the finite differences on degree k have leading coefficient k(k+1)/m, giving the stated spectrum; maximizing in the indicated scale regime uses monotonicity up to η=1/2. At fixed residue the same path works for every n, so the limit follows directly. The verification record, check.py and NumPy dependency were inspected; the finite diagnostics were not executed.
